name: Kumu Art Museum
funding: Part of the state-funded Art Museum of Estonia.
records_note: A thank-you page names about 30 funders and partners without a year and the About page lists the supervisory board; no reports or accounts.

name: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen
funding: 2024 income CHF 684k: Stadt St.Gallen 208k, Kanton 196k, other grants 165k (Swisslos, Pro Helvetia, foundations), members and Club der 20 CHF 105k. Raiffeisen funds education.
watch: Club der 20 members include UBS and Helvetia; Julius Bär and Würth are firm friends at CHF 500 to 1,500. Swisslos is a public lottery.
records_note: Annual reports 2016 to 2025 with full accounts, a funder page naming backers year by year to 2026, and a listed board.

name: Kunstfort bij Vijfhuizen
funding: Mondriaan Fund, Municipality of Haarlemmermeer, Province of North Holland; registered ANBI cultural foundation.
watch: UNESCO-listed military fortress converted into a center for contemporary art, ecological research and science fiction.

name: Kunsthal Charlottenborg
funding: Ministry of Culture, Statens Kunstfond and foundations including Augustinus Fonden, Det Obelske Familiefond, Ny Carlsberg, A.P. Møller, Bikuben, Knud Højgaard and William Demant.
watch: Augustinus Fonden's investment company holds over 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group, Obel's C.W. Obel A/S over 10% (May 2025). Both backed the 2025 programme.
records_note: Its parent academy posts annual reports for 2015 to 2025 with accounts that cover the Kunsthal, and the site lists 17 funders without a date.

name: Kunsthal Gent
funding: Flemish Community Cultural Department, City of Ghent; non-profit foundation.

name: Kunsthall Stavanger
watch: In Norway's oil capital; no Equinor or Aker BP link found.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2018 to 2025, an undated supporter list and its board; accounts for 2023 to 2025 sit in the Norwegian register.

name: Kunsthalle Bern
funding: Members, Förderkreise, Berner Kunstfonds, Stiftung Kunsthalle Bern, project foundations.
watch: Published an ethics code in June 2026.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2016 to 2025 with balance sheet and audit report, names funders in the 2025 thanks pages, and lists its board.

name: Kunsthalle Bremen
funding: Run by the Kunstverein in Bremen. Funders include Senator für Kultur, Senatskanzlei, Sparkasse Bremen, EY, Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung, Fritz Thyssen Stiftung, Hollweg Stiftung and Kaefer.
watch: Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung was set up in 1988 by the son of cigarette maker Hermann F. Reemtsma, so its money is tobacco-family money.
records_note: The Kunsthalle shows 22 funders as undated logos and publishes no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Kunsthalle Mainz
funding: Mainzer Stadtwerke and Mainzer Fernwärme head the partner list, with the City of Mainz, Volksbank Darmstadt-Mainz, Rheinhessen Sparkasse and a state ministry.
watch: Main partners are municipal utilities including gas-fired district heating.
records_note: The Kunsthalle names 14 partners with Mainzer Stadtwerke first, but posts no annual report, accounts or board, and its operating foundation lists no officers.

name: Kunsthalle Münster
funding: Municipal institution of the City of Münster's Kulturamt. Residence NRW+ fellowships are paid equally by the NRW culture ministry and Kunststiftung NRW, with Pro Helvetia. A Freundeskreis helps.
watch: No Stadtwerke or arms funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Part of the City of Münster's culture office; the city posts annual accounts 2010 to 2024, while the Kunsthalle lists no funders or board.

name: Kunsthalle Tbilisi
funding: Roving space founded 2018 by Irena Popiashvili and Lika Chkuaseli; mostly private donors with a small municipal share (unnamed).
watch: No donors are named on its site.
records_note: Its archived site has one About paragraph naming two founders; no reports, accounts, supporters or board appear.

name: Kunsthalle Zürich
funding: Funded by members and patrons, City of Zürich and Canton Zürich subsidies, the Ernst Göhner, Foksal Gallery, Gubler Hablützel and Luma foundations, and Ringier AG.
watch: Swiss Re and Bloomberg, named in the old note, are not on the 2025 supporter list. No controversy found among the funders listed.
records_note: Annual reports 2015 to 2025 include audited accounts; a dated 2025 supporter list and the full board are on the about page.
